correctness.rationale: The exact Green kernel of JJ* folds into explicit even/odd Green blocks and a rank-one cross block; inversion of the mixed endpoints yields cos z-a cos(a z)=0. The Laguerre-Polya product sin z-sin(az) implies all zeros real, and a direct simultaneous-root contradiction proves simplicity. The exceptional parameters are solved by separated boundary conditions. Hadamard factorization identifies the entire function with the true trace-class Fredholm determinant. Comparing its quadratic and quartic coefficients rigorously classifies all real-parameter equal spectra. The regular second-order block eigenvalue counting and finite-rank perturbation inequality give n s_n -> max(1,|a|)/pi, proving Schatten and logarithmic-residue limits. The package checker replayed 472 finite/root/coefficient consistency assertions; these are supporting tests, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Primary full text of Lyubich--Tsedenbayar (2010) concerns polynomials phi(J), so neither its I+aJ transcendental equations nor its general results include the reflected Hankel term RJ. Eveson (2004) concerns Volterra iterates, with reflection used only for a different norm bound. Tuan--Gorenflo (1996) treats one-sided triangular kernels. The published reflection-symmetric weighted-integration comparison result uses a rank-one correction J_w-alpha Q_w, not infinite-rank output reflection RJ. Semantic searches for both the exact determinant and isospectral parameters, as well as the accessible own ledger, found no mathematical implication covering the combined determinant and unique isospectral pair; priority remains subject to obscure literature risk.

value.rationale: Determines the entire singular spectrum of the structurally natural mixture of causal Volterra and output-reflected Hankel Volterra integration, including a distinctive exact isospectral ambiguity that is invisible in the constant leading approximation-number coefficient. The complete real-parameter rigidity classification and the entire plateau of identical weak-Schatten constants distinguish quantitative spectral identifiability from coarse asymptotics. Fredholm determinant and all positive singular values are reusable for best finite-rank approximation, conditioning and operator-ideal boundaries. Not merely a one-parameter numerical norm calculation.
